title: Fault-aware control
equipment: High-zone pumping station with redundant pressure, suction level, and drive feedback
objective: Detect, isolate, degrade, and recover from supported device faults.
physicalPurpose: Maintain justified local pump authority when connected sensors and the drive update at different rates or fail independently.

simplifications: The paired header paths use first-order pressure dynamics rather than full pump curves and hydraulic-network dynamics.
The pressure predictor uses the declared nominal Euler model and does not establish diagnostic coverage outside its qualified region.
Sensor and actuator faults are deterministic Simulation events rather than physical failure evidence.
Cybersecurity, electrical protection, cavitation physics, voting with more than two devices, and every common-cause failure remain outside this lesson.

baseline.limitation: A timely in-range but biased pressure value silently moves the naive controller because quality and freshness alone cannot establish correctness.

change.decision: Continue with one isolated healthy pressure transmitter only when the model relation identifies the failed device; otherwise remove automatic authority and require cause removal, acknowledgement, healthy qualification, and approved reset.

disturbances: Add +1.0 bar bias to pressure transmitter A while quality remains good.
Remove both pressure qualities, withhold level updates until stale, and deliver a fresh 19 percent low-level sample in restored cases.
Stick the protected header actuator and independent drive-feedback path while requesting a pressure increase, then release it before supervised recovery.

acceptance.window: first biased pressure sample through isolated degraded mode
ambiguous pressure, stale level, low level, and confirmed actuator fault

abortPredicates: A required value, timestamp, residual, pressure, level, request, application, or feedback is nonfinite or outside its declared hard range.
The device intervals, freshness limits, fault schedule, model, controller, substep, seed, limits, or evidence class changes without declaration.
An isolated or ineligible pressure drives the protected controller, an ambiguous or critical fault retains automatic authority, or a reset clears an unqualified fault.
Approved restoration exceeds 10 percent per second.
safety.restorationMode: Remove automatic authority for critical faults, record acknowledgement separately, require ten healthy station scans, then accept an explicit reset and rate-limit restored pump speed.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised pumping-station controls engineer with instrumentation, electrical, hydraulic, operations, network and safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical pump, drive, reservoir, pressure transmitter, level transmitter, gateway, or network is operated.
Simulation fault injection does not establish physical diagnostic coverage or proof-test intervals.
Physical application requires reviewed device independence, common-cause analysis, protection layers, safe-state hydraulics, commissioning and explicit approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Distinguish detection, isolation, degradation, safe state, acknowledgement, cause removal, qualification, and reset on a multirate pumping station.
requiredVisibleEvidence: two pressure sensors and model predictor

learning.context: Two fast pressure transmitters, one slow level transmitter, and independent drive feedback provide different evidence at different intervals.
learning.reason: Timely ordered communication cannot establish that a sensor value is correct or that the actuator followed its command.
theory: Multirate resampling retains timestamps and ages instead of pretending held values are new.
Physical redundancy reveals disagreement; analytical model redundancy supplies the third relation needed for bounded isolation.
A slow safety constraint uses both freshness and conservative projection.
Detection, isolation, degradation, safe state, acknowledgement, qualification, and reset are distinct decisions.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict pressure-A isolation on the third 100 ms biased sample, actuator confirmation on the third 200 ms mismatched feedback, immediate low-level trip, ten healthy recovery scans, and at most 10 percent-per-second restoration.
practicalPreparation: Verify all device intervals, timestamps, freshness and plausibility limits, residual thresholds, counters, fault priority, safe output, recovery authority, plant records, aborts and Simulation label.
Record the expected mode, isolated component and fault code before each injection.
learning.baseline: Run the naive controller from pressure transmitter A without redundancy or actuator supervision.
learning.change: Run the fault-aware controller from the qualified selected pressure with multirate supervision, degradation, safe modes and supervised recovery.
learning.comparison: Compare false trips, isolation and confirmation latency, wrong selections, pressure deviation, safe-output timing, service availability and restoration rate.
learning.validation: Prove healthy, biased-sensor, single-loss, ambiguous-pressure, stale-level, low-level, stuck-actuator, acknowledgement, premature-reset and approved-recovery behavior against independent oracles.
learning.explanation: Trace each device from update interval and source timestamp through age, plausibility, residual, counter, isolation, authority, command, feedback and plant response.
